_doc: 🔴 F1 FALSIFIER — THE BINDING EMIT-LIST. Author: proposer6, 2026-08-19. Spec: docs/02_METHOD_SPEC.md §39.32(h), merge condition granted by the lead.
_why_this_file_exists_here: F1 is being MERGED into engineer6's §R38.5 endpoint pilot, because three lines of reasoning
converged on 'we need one real complete run'. 🔴 A MERGE IS THE STANDARD WAY A FALSIFIER
VANISHES WHILE EVERYONE BELIEVES IT RAN. If this list lived only in a method document, the
merged pilot would report cost and convergence, everyone would tick F1 off, and the falsifier
It sits BESIDE qc_levels.json on purpose (ADR-080's own mechanism): the requirement and the
route templates it constrains cannot drift apart silently if they are in the same directory.
_binding_rule: 🔴 IF THE MERGED PILOT REPORTS ONLY COST AND CONVERGENCE, F1 HAS NOT BEEN RUN — whatever the merge document says. A missing observable here is not a degraded result; it is an ABSENT result, and it must be reported as absent rather than inferred from what did arrive.

required_observables.emit: ∠Li–O=C at the CONVERGED endpoint geometry, in degrees, for BOTH endpoints
required_observables.external_reference: experimental ≈138(2)° — 🔴 EXTERNAL to this project, therefore not something we could have constructed. That is why the falsifier is attached to it (§39.36(a)).

required_observables.emit: the five ring bond lengths C1-O2, C1-O5, O2-C3, C4-O5, C3-C4 at the converged geometry, in Å
required_observables.external_reference: crystallographic cyclic carbonate: C(sp2)-O 1.33-1.36, O-CH2 1.44-1.46, C-C ≈1.52 (ADR-066). No molecule has five equal ring bonds.

required_observables.emit: the number of negative Hessian eigenvalues at the geometry ENTERING the tight stage (= stage-1 exit under the ADR-099 two-stage protocol; = the raw guess if a single-stage run is ever done)
required_observables.cost: 🟢 FREE, AND ALREADY PAID. Stage 2's CalcFC IS a Hessian at stage-1's exit geometry, computed at step 1 before anything moves. We already have this number in every run; the only thing missing was that nobody emitted it. See §39.38(c).
required_observables.answers: (i) whether the symmetric (C2v, ∠=180.00°) point was a saddle AT ALL -- if n_imag == 0 here, proposer6's diagnosis is wrong and the guesses were adequate (§39.32(h) F1); (ii) 🔴 whether STAGE 1 STAYED ON THE SYMMETRY ELEMENT -- the cheapest possible detection of the two-stage failure mode, reported BEFORE a single tight cycle is spent.

required_observables.emit: the number of negative Hessian eigenvalues at the converged geometry, counting EVERY negative eigenvalue with no magnitude waiver
the point group AT STEP 1 and AT CONVERGENCE, as data
required_observables.why: STATE §0-g's standing order: symmetry breaking must be a MEASUREMENT, not an assumption. 🔴 Also the only direct check that `nosymm` did its job (B-2): if the group is re-detected and re-imposed, the C-9 perturbation was undone and every log still says 'converged'.

required_observables.emit: ⟨S²⟩ before AND after annihilation, at BOTH stages (rough=선택된 시작점의 로그, tight), as NUMBERS — no verdict (C-3). Doublet clean value 0.75.
required_observables.why: 🔴 §39.42(a) REQUIRED EMISSION (proposer7, 2026-08-20): a reduced EC radical is exactly the class where a UKS reference contaminates, and an 'endpoint' with a badly contaminated reference is not the species we think we certified — nothing else in the chain would notice. GFN2 has no ⟨S²⟩; this is a DFT-stage observable only.
required_observables.wired_as: f1_observables.json fields s2_stage1_rough / s2_stage2_tight (payload/endpoint_prep.sh, criteria/g16.py::parse_s2). coder10, 2026-08-20.

required_observables.emit: point group AND ∠Li–O=C AND the max out-of-plane deviation, AT STAGE-1 EXIT
required_observables.cost: 🟢 FREE — purely geometric, computed from the stage-1 output .xyz. No job.
required_observables.why: 🔴 ADR-099 two-stage: if stage 1 runs without `nosymm`, G16 re-imposes the point group, the C-9 perturbation is undone at step 1, and stage 2 inherits the pristine symmetric structure. Stage-1 exit is where that is cheapest to see. §39.38(a)/(c), lead's point 3.
required_observables.binding: a stage-1 exit whose point group is NOT C1 is a DEFECT REPORT about our route, not a fact about the molecule.

_also_required_by_other_constraints_not_.irc_untruncated: 🔴 NOT an F1 item, listed so it is not dropped as 'extra': C-2 ALREADY requires both IRC directions with normal_termination, n_points >= 5 and |E_end - E_TS| > 0.05 eV. An untruncated TS+IRC run is therefore a precondition of U-56 condition 7 (§39.32(g)) and is NOT new scope — the same shape as C-9's 'optimise in C1' having been an unimplemented adopted decision.
_also_required_by_other_constraints_not_.abort_status: a wall-clock abort is `budget_exhausted`, NEVER `non_converged`, and must not enter any convergence or success rate (§39.34(b), lead-ratified).

_provenance: [SPEC] — this file states a requirement. It contains NO measured values and no estimates. Cf. §39.36(c): a number's provenance token must exist before it can be honest; [FIXTURE] is proposed there as the missing fourth token.
_two_stage_note: 🔴 ADR-099 (user): rough opt -> tight opt+freq. The C-9 perturbation is applied ONCE, BEFORE stage 1, and is NOT re-applied between stages. `nosymm` is required on BOTH stages (`endpoint_opt_rough` and `endpoint_opt_freq` both belong in `_nosymm_required_job_types`). Rough = SAME functional/basis/solvent/GRID as tight; only the convergence thresholds differ. §39.38.
